contract: Message streams (published Server 2.11.1, MessageStreamController and MessageStreamService over the Workflow package's runtime-reserved signal). Cluster info publishes the message streams contract and the worker capability the same contract with supported true. A client appends ordered messages to a named stream of a workflow instance: the first message is position 1, a repeated message id with the same payload is a duplicate at its original position, and with another payload a 409 message_identity_conflict. Each accepted message reaches the current run as a __durable_workflow_message_stream SignalReceived whose single argument holds the message schema, stream name, message id, position and the inline payload envelope. Refused requests are counted as malformed without keeping their payload, by a diagnostic message id. Diagnostics list every stream of the instance by name with positions, pending counts, the pending wait, duplicate and malformed counts and the last input, without payloads. A worker on protocol 1.15 or newer reports open receives with message_stream_waits and consumed messages with message_stream_cursors on a workflow task completion; the server checks both before the completion changes anything, records MessageCursorAdvanced for each moved cursor and clears the wait. An open condition wait is woken by a stream message, which it consumes without SignalApplied. When the run continues as new, the next run receives a payload-free cursor checkpoint for each acknowledged stream and every unconsumed message again, in append order; signals the old run had not consumed are rejected. Appends to a closed run are refused with run_not_active, duplicates included. Embedded applications have no HTTP message streams.
